notes: Wealth manager podcast notes with no performance figures; issues are a retirement-income guarantee, a one-sided interval fund takeaway and an undisclosed client quote, against a fully disclosed third-party list designation.

planted.span: the Kettleby Rowan income framework is built so that our retired clients never have to worry about running out of money, no matter what the markets do.
planted.explanation: It is an absolute outcome promise that no income plan can substantiate, amounting to an implied guarantee against market risk.

planted.span: Interval funds give individual investors a simple way into private credit: higher yields than most public bond funds, steady quarterly distributions and far less of the day-to-day price movement you see in stocks.
planted.explanation: It lists only benefits and never mentions limited quarterly repurchases, credit and default risk, leverage, fees or appraisal-based valuation, and the generic loss-of-principal line in the disclosures does not supply that balance.

planted.span: After thirty years of watching our 401(k)s bounce around, Elise and I finally sleep at night. Kettleby Rowan built us an income plan that just works.
planted.explanation: The quote is attributed to a named person with no disclosure of whether he is a client, whether he was compensated, or any resulting conflict of interest.

decoys.span: Kettleby Rowan Wealth Advisors was named to the Garthside Advisor Review 2026 list of Top Fee-Only Advisers, published April 14, 2026. The list was compiled and tabulated by Garthside Advisor Review from data for the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, weighing assets under management, client retention and regulatory history. Kettleby Rowan did not pay to be considered for the list; it pays Garthside Advisor Review a $1,950 annual licensing fee to display the designation in its marketing materials. The designation is not indicative of future performance or of any individual client's experience.
decoys.why_ok: The paragraph gives the publication date, the twelve-month period the list was based on, the rater that compiled and tabulated it, and the $1,950 licensing fee the firm pays.
